title: Check: Reactions of Acids with Metals

questions.stem: What are the products when a metal reacts with an acid?
questions.explanation: When a metal reacts with an acid, the products are a salt and hydrogen gas. The general equation is: Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen. This is different from neutralisation, which produces salt and water.

questions.stem: Why does copper not react with dilute hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series
Copper is a transition metal so it never reacts

questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, meaning it is less reactive than hydrogen. Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from acids. Copper cannot give its electrons to H⁺ ions.
